general_query_list.answer: Technical meeting chaired by Arjun in Priya's absence. Legal classified maintenance records as personal data that must stay in India, so the team agreed to keep AWS but deploy everything, including backups, in the Mumbai region. Because checklists vary by truck model, the engineering team decided to store work orders for the scheduling service in MongoDB, with a nightly export for reporting. Early access to the telematics API works and the 1 February go-live was confirmed. For fleet customers who want to see service status, the team agreed on a responsive web portal rather than a native iPhone app, as a later phase.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Priya's out today, she asked me to run this one. Let's keep it quick. First, Sara has something on hosting.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Sara
meeting_transcripts.content: Yes. Legal came back on the maintenance records. Because they include driver names and incident reports, they count as personal data, and our policy now is that personal data stays in India. So FleetCare can't just sit in any region.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: We're currently in US East because that's the default the account came with.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Sara
meeting_transcripts.content: That would have to change before the pilot.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Mumbai is the obvious one. ap-south-1. Everything we use is available there.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Meera
meeting_transcripts.content: Latency from Pune is better too.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Does moving it delay anything?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: A couple of days. We haven't got production data in yet, so now's the time.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: So, we stay with AWS, but everything gets deployed in the Mumbai region. Sara, does that satisfy legal?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Sara
meeting_transcripts.content: Yes, as long as backups also stay in Mumbai.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Backups too. Okay, done.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Second thing. The work orders. My team's been building the job templates, and every truck model has a different checklist. A Tata has a different service checklist from an Ashok Leyland, and the trailers are different again. The fields keep changing.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Meera
meeting_transcripts.content: That's going to be messy to report on.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Right. So the team's view is that we store work orders in MongoDB. Each work order is one document with whatever checklist it needs. It's just simpler for this data.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Whatever makes it faster, honestly.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Meera
meeting_transcripts.content: Can I still query it?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Yes, there's a connector, and we'll export nightly to your reporting side.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Meera
meeting_transcripts.content: Okay, then fine by me.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Alright, work orders go in MongoDB for the scheduling service then. I'll get the team started on the data model this week.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Next, the timeline. Where are we?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: The telematics vendor sent us early access to the new API on Tuesday. It works. So we're still on track for the first of February, no change there.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Good, I've told the Pune depot manager February first.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Yes, February first stands. Confirmed.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Meera
meeting_transcripts.content: The data import is about seventy percent done. The Pune spreadsheets were the worst.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Sorry.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Meera
meeting_transcripts.content: Ha, not your fault.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: One more. Customer service asked whether customers could see their trucks' service status, the fleet customers who lease from us. They wanted an iPhone app.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Customers on iPhones, sure, a lot of them.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: I don't want to build a native iOS app for that. A customer portal that's a responsive website works on iPhones and anything else.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Sara
meeting_transcripts.content: Customer-facing means a separate login and a separate review from me.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Understood. So the customer service-status portal is web-based and responsive, no native app. It's a later phase, but let's agree the direction.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Meera
meeting_transcripts.content: Agreed.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Yep.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Okay, thanks. I'll send notes to Priya.
